      <title>Mystery over source of Ebola infection in Nigeria fuels concern about spread of virus</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/23/ebola-swiss-patient-nigeria-dr-congo-concerns-virus-spread</link>
      <description><p>Switzerland says patient is wife of Swiss diplomat and believed to have contracted virus while travelling in Uganda</p><p>Health officials across Africa are racing to determine how Nigeria’s first Ebola patient ⁠in more than a decade ⁠became infected, amid fears ​the outbreak could spread further after reaching a fourth African country.</p><p>The Swiss foreign ministry said on Friday the patient in Nigeria, the Ugandan-born wife of a Swiss diplomat based in Abuja, had not travelled to the Democratic Republic of ⁠Congo, where the outbreak was first detected in mid-May before spreading to Uganda, Kenya and now Nigeria. The woman was believed to have contracted Ebola while travelling with her husband in Uganda, the ministry added.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/23/ebola-swiss-patient-nigeria-dr-congo-concerns-virus-spread">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Lewis Hamilton aims to extend career till early 2030s so he can race in African Grand Prix</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/oct/22/lewis-hamilton-aims-to-extend-career-till-early-2030s-so-he-can-race-in-african-grand-prix</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>41-year-old set on ‘dream to be able to race in Africa’</p></li><li><p>Rwanda to host despite criticism of human rights record</p></li></ul><p>Lewis Hamilton has said he hopes to remain racing in Formula One until he can take part in the African Grand Prix which is <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/oct/13/f1-returns-to-africa-for-first-time-since-1993-with-10-year-rwanda-deal-from-early-2030s">set to take place in Rwanda in the 2030s</a>. The seven-time world champion believes it is right that F1 is to hold a race there despite criticism of the country’s human rights record.</p><p>Last week F1 confirmed Rwanda was to host the African Grand Prix having concluded a 10-year agreement for the meeting on a purpose-built circuit, with the first race set for the early 2030s. It is lined up to be held on a circuit in Bugesera, 25 miles south of the capital, Kigali, which has yet to be constructed and marks a return to the African continent for the first time since it last held a race at Kyalami, South Africa in 1993.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/oct/22/lewis-hamilton-aims-to-extend-career-till-early-2030s-so-he-can-race-in-african-grand-prix">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/21/us-vaccine-trial-african-newborns-hepatitis-b</link>
      <description><p>Hepatitis B study in Guinea-Bissau that was to be funded by CDC and that drew global backlash ‘will not move forward’</p><p>The US-backed hepatitis B vaccine trial in African newborns that drew global backlash was halted, the lead researcher said on Wednesday.</p><p>It was “now clear” that the study “will not move forward in Guinea-Bissau”, Frederik Schaltz-Buchholzer, a Danish researcher, <a href="https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/missed-opportunity-guinea-bissaus-children-why-trial-frederik-wttde/">wrote</a> on LinkedIn, adding, “we were not given the necessary governmental approval.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/21/us-vaccine-trial-african-newborns-hepatitis-b">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Severely ill ICE detainees face imminent deportation to unknown African states, advocates say</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/21/ice-detention-illness-deportation-florida</link>
      <description><p>Flights to third countries where the detainees have no ties are scheduled as early as Wednesday, relatives detail</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/15/immigration-trump-midterms-reader-q-a">Send us your questions about immigration and the midterms</a></p></li></ul><p>Relatives of gravely ill detainees at two <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/florida">Florida</a> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/usimmigration">immigration</a> jails say authorities are about to deport their loved ones to unknown countries in Africa despite worsening medical conditions.</p><p>Flights are scheduled as early as Wednesday, according to the families and the immigration advocacy group the Workers Circle, which has been monitoring conditions and speaking with detainees inside two <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/ice-us-immigration-and-customs-enforcement">Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)</a> facilities in south Florida.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/21/ice-detention-illness-deportation-florida">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Case in Africa’s most populous country was detected in a woman who had travelled from Uganda</p><p>Nigeria has confirmed an Ebola case in its capital, Abuja, after a woman who arrived from Uganda tested positive for the virus, the health ministry said.</p><p>The woman began showing symptoms on 7 October and was admitted to a hospital in Abuja four days later, where she was later diagnosed with Ebola. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 16:23:41 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category></category><title>West Bank: Extensive military operation 'on the way', Netanyahu says</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261023-west-bank-extensive-military-operation-on-the-way-netanyahu-says</link><description>
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday warned of an imminent large-scale military operation in the West Bank and vowed to displace some residents of Hebron after Palestinian gunmen killed two soldiers in an attack.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/be36cda4-cef9-11f1-b713-5b4a75578ebb/w:1024/p:16x9/West-Bank-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/be36cda4-cef9-11f1-b713-5b4a75578ebb/w:1024/p:16x9/West-Bank-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f0a1d4d0-cef6-11f1-ac7e-8f6e4b6af7d6</guid><pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 15:56:28 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Middle East</category><title>Yes, Israeli settlers are ripping up West Bank olive trees – but this video is fake</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20261023-yes-israeli-settlers-ripping-up-west-bank-olive-trees-%E2%80%93-but-this-video-fake</link><description>
Israeli settlers and soldiers have made a habit of destroying olive trees grown by Palestinian farmers in the West Bank and, in recent days, a video showing some trees being ripped up has circulated online. Just one problem: this particular video was generated by artificial intelligence. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2ffdb4-cef6-11f1-93cf-bdb9616e85cf/w:1024/p:16x9/ban-olivier2-EN.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2ffdb4-cef6-11f1-93cf-bdb9616e85cf/w:1024/p:16x9/ban-olivier2-EN.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">292a3e12-cef4-11f1-9d05-d19f7e65e183</guid><pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 15:56:19 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2ffdb4-cef6-11f1-93cf-bdb9616e85cf/w:1024/p:16x9/ban-olivier2-EN.jpg">© X</source><dc:creator>The FRANCE 24 Observers</dc:creator></item><item><category>arts24</category><title>AKAA art and design fair brings African artists to Paris</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/arts24/20261023-akaa-art-and-design-fair-brings-african-artists-to-paris</link><description>
Every year the art and design fair AKAA, or "Also Known as Africa", brings dozens of African and Afro-descendant artists to the French capital. As the 11th edition gets underway, we welcome Nigerian painter Midegbeyan Ojisua and South African artist Olivié Keck.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/716031c6-cee7-11f1-8f1a-bdb9616e85cf/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-94ad43c0.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/716031c6-cee7-11f1-8f1a-bdb9616e85cf/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-94ad43c0.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cbff6ccc-cef2-11f1-9794-2bb3a7226ba0</guid><pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 15:13:37 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Alison SARGENT</dc:creator></item><item><category>Talking Europe</category><title>Europe faces threat of organised sabotage, terrorist attacks: Estonian FM Tsahkna</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/talking-europe/20261023-europe-faces-threat-of-organised-sabotage-terrorist-attacks-estonian-fm-tsahkna</link><description>
Estonia's counterintelligence service has recently warned that sabotage operations orchestrated by Russian special services have reached a new and dangerous phase in Europe, with targets no longer being purely symbolic. Talking Europe sits down with the country's foreign minister, Margus Tsahkna, to discuss the security situation in Estonia and the European Union in general.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ea372b5c-ce35-11f1-b2a4-97baf3e9dd31/w:1024/p:16x9/TALKING-EUROPE-MARGUS-TSAHKNA.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ea372b5c-ce35-11f1-b2a4-97baf3e9dd31/w:1024/p:16x9/TALKING-EUROPE-MARGUS-TSAHKNA.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">55569ad4-cc70-11f1-bde3-7d1b056370b1</guid><pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 14:55:15 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Armen GEORGIAN</dc:creator></item><item><category>Talking Europe</category><title>EU member states wrangle over all-important budget: Is a deal this year feasible?</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/talking-europe/20261023-eu-member-states-wrangle-over-all-important-budget-is-a-deal-this-year-feasible</link><description>
A marathon EU summit on October 15-16 failed to produce a breakthrough on the European Union's next long-term budget. Although EU leaders put on a brave face at the end of the talks by saying that "the way forward is clearer", EU capitals appear deadlocked on what that path is. At stake is the EU's ability to finance its strategic priorities from 2028 to 2034. The main dividing line is between the so-called "frugal countries", who want deep cuts to the proposed budget, and the "friends of cohesion", who say that cuts are not the answer.

<![CDATA[ Latest from Space.com ]]> https://www.space.com/feeds.xml Fri, 23 Oct 2026 16:00:00 +0000 en <![CDATA[ Never finishing the fight: Where did Xbox go wrong with Halo? ]]> Halo: Campaign Evolved was Xbox’s second attempt at refreshing the 2001 sci-fi FPS classic, and it is perfectly fine. A cromulent remake, if ever there was one, but it’s hardly a franchise-saver, especially as Xbox looks to rethink its studio structure and approach to renowned IPs like Halo or Gears of War.

Halo hasn’t been the same since original developer Bungie — now owned by Sony and working on Destiny and Marathon — departed, leaving 343 Industries (now Halo Studios) to guide the franchise.

Neither Halo 4 nor 5 meaningfully evolved the gameplay formula or overarching narrative. Halo Infinite found more success by reheating what “old Halo felt like” and sticking it into a half-baked open world, but it still felt far from the series’ glory days.

This year’s full remake of Combat Evolved's campaign delivered exactly what it promised: a shiny, 2026 version of the game that made audiences fall in love with the franchise. It was a clear attempt to reignite faith in 343’s vision, but how is a faithful, shinier remake proof of anything?

It might not even matter anymore, as the new Xbox leadership has rocked the ship again, leaving Master Chief and the universe’s future cloudier than ever before. Now, with rumors of a reboot being considered at new steward Activision, is there hope for the Spartans, or will Xbox run into another dead end?

Rebooted or not, Halo needs to leave Master Chief behind

It looks like the ‘Halo Studios’ moniker only lasted a single (remade) game, as Xbox has recently announced that Call of Duty maker and publisher Activision — which houses many FPS-oriented studios — is taking over development, essentially leaving the 343 veterans as a minor support studio, which translates into more layoffs.

If we put aside the human and institutional cost of this whole back-and-forth over the years (a big ask in today’s climate), there are reasons to be optimistic about the quality of an Activision-developed Halo. Regardless of what you think about the Call of Duty IP in 2026 and the publisher’s overall vision for it, it’s clear there’s plenty of talent holding everything together and, more importantly, enough experience to iterate on what Halo’s multiplayer side needs to shine bright again.

But this won’t fix the larger issue with Halo, which is that Master Chief should’ve been left behind long ago. Like it or not, it’s difficult to deny Halo’s “golden era” ended with Halo: Reach (Bungie’s swansong under Xbox) and the Halo Wars spinoffs, which took the series into the real-time strategy genre. These games were wildly different, but they had one core thing in common: they made the sci-fi setting feel bigger instead of smaller, offering the perfect blueprint to build upon in a post-Halo 3 world.

There’s nothing inherently wrong with the Master Chief. Franchises can be built around iconic characters like Mario or Lara Croft. But in the post-Bungie era, his role changed from an extremely competent Spartan soldier to a space messiah. Halo 4, 5, and Infinite used sci-fi nonsense to transform him into this larger-than-life figure, rendering the rest of the UNSC largely powerless in the process.

It’s the same mistake ID Software made with Doomguy, centering the story on how super special he is, and not on the world he inhabits. Now rumours are rumbling that Activision’s reboot might focus on Chief’s origins; that's the last thing Halo needs.

Are Halo 2 and 3 remakes happening?

Forgetting Activision’s next Halo for a second, we were teased with (even if there wasn’t an official confirmation from Xbox) at least a Halo 2 remake via Halo: Campaign Evolved’s alternative ending.

Back in May 2026, renowned insider Rebs Gaming confidently reported that Halo 2 and 3 remakes were in development. But can fans realistically expect them after new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma’s latest shakeup?

Halo Studios could have done a "fine" job with safe remakes of the two original Halo sequels while Activision handles new projects. It’s hard to reject that approach, especially after Xbox finding success with Bethesda’s The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered and confirming two Fallout remasters are in the works. It seems like money waiting to be made, but the remakes could be cooked too.

Xbox and 343/Halo Studios have made plenty of mistakes with Halo, but the killer has always been their lack of conviction in their ideas. And look, nostalgia shouldn’t be the driving force behind a franchise in dire need of reinvention, but I’m far more annoyed by the creative rollbacks, flip-flopping, and now the loss of knowledge and talent accompanying the gutting of Halo Studios.

Xbox Live Action

We haven’t even touched on the mess that was the live-action Halo show. It lasted only two seasons, had John-117 walking around outside the Mjolnir armor for most of its runtime, and was cancelled just as the story finally got to the titular Halo. Why would you stray so far from the source material, and how do you miss the mark so badly?

In many ways, it perfectly encapsulated what’s been wrong with Halo as a whole for so many years. The powers that be can’t decide what they really want from it, and thus it’s stuck, unable to leave the past behind or convincingly establish a new horizon for itself. Other franchises have run into the same issues — looking at you, Star Wars — but Halo has been stuck in this purgatory for 15+ years, as Xbox leaders and strategy shifts come and go.

Could Xbox’s newly-formed XP division deliver the focused big-screen adaptation the series has always deserved? I’m sure that’s the plan, but even a cursory glance back at Xbox’s handling of the franchise for the past decade or so says no.

Halo’s deep problems won’t be fixed overnight, and throwing a bunch of hard-working developers to the curb certainly won’t help. Halo’s current struggles didn’t come from Halo Studios or 343 Industries; they came from impatient and incompetent leadership calling the property-defining shots. I’ve seen nothing to suggest that’s changed.

]]> <![CDATA[ Private Griffin moon lander gets put to the test | Space photo of the day for Oct. 23, 2026 ]]>

The robotic Griffin lunar lander has passed a host of critical tests ahead of its first-ever moon mission, which is scheduled to launch later this year.

What is it?

At NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California, Voyager Technologies' Griffin Mission One (or Griffin-1) lunar lander has gone through an absolute gauntlet of tests. The spacecraft was put through environmental testing that explored how the vehicle will fare in the extreme conditions it will experience on its ride to the surface of the moon.

This testing simulated the extreme temperatures, shaking and even the sounds that the spacecraft will experience from launch to landing. And, as JPL announced recently, the lander passed this series of tests with flying colors, as we can see in this image snapped Aug. 31 of the lander inside the 25-foot-wide (7.6 meters) space simulator at JPL.

"NASA JPL’s Environmental Test Laboratory has been putting robotic explorers to the test since the Ranger program gave us NASA’s first up-close views of the moon's surface in the mid-1960s. We’re proud to provide our expertise and facilities to support this new phase of commercial lunar exploration," Charles Whetsel, manager for the Exploration Systems Development Office at JPL, said in a statement.

Why is it incredible?

Griffin-1 is expected to launch to the moon later this year as part of NASA's CLPS (Commercial Lunar Payload Services) initiative. The spacecraft will carry over 1,100 pounds (455 kilograms) of cargo to its landing site near the lunar south pole.

In this cargo will be science experiments and new technologies that will be tested on the moon's surface, including Astrolab's FLIP rover, which will explore the lunar surface with a history-making supercomputer onboard.

This suite of experimental hardware won't just expand our understanding of the moon up close. Griffin-1's exploration will also help set the stage for a future, crewed moon base, which NASA aims to build near the south pole over the next half-decade or so.

]]> <![CDATA[ 'Stupendously large black holes' aren't a major component of dark matter, study finds ]]> Black holes more massive than entire galaxies are not a major component of the mysterious dark matter that's thought to make up most of the matter in the cosmos, a new study finds.

For decades, to explain why galaxies do not spin apart at the speeds at which they whirl, scientists have suggested the existence of an unseen substance known as dark matter, whose gravitational pull helps keep galaxies together. Dark matter is thought to make up about five-sixths of all matter in the universe.

Much remains unknown about dark matter, however — including whether or not it actually exists. Black holes make good potential contenders for dark matter, since they are extremely massive and are difficult to spot in the dark depths of space.

In the new study, researchers investigated whether dark matter could be made of "stupendously large black holes," ones with masses greater than 100 billion times the mass of the sun. Stupendously large black holes greater than 1 million billion to 10 million billion suns in mass would be heavier than entire galaxies.

So far, astronomers have not detected any stupendously large black holes — currently, the largest black hole known may weigh about 36 billion suns. Since researchers have not seen any even after looking at many galaxies, the new study noted they cannot make up all of dark matter — but team members wondered if the exotic objects still might constitute a significant portion of the puzzling substance.

Often, dark matter is thought of "as a fine dust spread everywhere," study co-author Christopher Gerlach, a theoretical physicist at the Mainz Institute for Theoretical Physics in Germany, told Space.com. However, if dark matter is packed into a handful of gigantic objects such as stupendously large black holes, "the universe becomes grainy on very large scales. And we can check that."

Specifically, the scientists analyzed the light from the dawn of the universe, study co-author Yann Gouttenoire, a theoretical physicist at the Mainz Institute for Theoretical Physics, told Space.com.

For the first 380,000 years after the Big Bang, the cosmos was filled with a hot plasma in which light was trapped. Eventually, the expansion of the universe let the cosmos cool enough for the plasma to largely dissipate and form atoms. This in turn let light shine freely, "and that light is still arriving today," Gerlach explained. "We call it the cosmic microwave background, a snapshot of the infant universe covering the whole sky."

]]> <![CDATA[ Space debris: Are we on track for true sustainability? (op-ed) ]]> David Zamora is the chairman of the Space Data Association. He contributed this article to Space.com's Expert Voices: Op-Ed & Insights.

The commercialization of space is well underway, and as a result, Earth’s orbit is becoming ever more congested. The current number of active satellites in orbit stands at around 16,000, according to the European Space Agency( ESA), and this number is expected to jump close to 60,000 by 2035, Novaspace projects. While it’s not always given the recognition it deserves, space has fast become a critical infrastructure layer, underpinning nearly all systems that enable modern life as we know it. Therefore, it’s critical that a safe and clean operating landscape is maintained.

Yet this is becoming increasingly challenging, particularly given that, alongside the rapid increase in space traffic, there are also more than 1.2 million pieces of debris over 1 centimeter (0.4 inches) cm in Earth’s orbit, each of which could damage satellites and spacecraft and potentially cause disastrous consequences. With the number of active satellites and debris objects in space continuing to increase, the space environment is under growing pressure.

Balancing expansion with sustainability

Space was once the sole domain of nation states, but this is no longer the case. As technology has advanced, launch costs have decreased, and satellites have become more efficient, smaller and cheaper to build. These changes have democratized space, resulting in a massive increase in space traffic, not least constellations in low Earth orbit (LEO) that comprise thousands of satellites.

Plans are underway to further expand these constellations, and new and even bigger constellations are also expected to launch in the coming years. Added to that, we’re also likely to see the first space-based data centers within the next few years, which may well mark the start of the wholesale shift of data centers from Earth to space, which will further add to the congestion already being felt.

To ensure that space continues to meet our current and future needs, this continued expansion must happen in a sustainable way. Maintaining a safe and clean landscape is more important than ever before, and mitigating the impact of space debris is critical to that effort.

Maintaining a safe environment

Mitigating the impact of debris involves a multipronged approach. Whether intentional or unintentional, the creation of new space debris by future space missions must be minimized as much as possible. This applies during launch, operation, and end of life phases, and satellites and other spacecraft need to be designed with this in mind. Additionally, satellites that are no longer active should not remain in orbit for extended periods, because this only increases the chance of collision events which would create new debris. The standard rule has been 25 years, but there are recommendations now that this should be lowered to five years.

Also critical is the prevention of in-orbit collisions between active satellites and other objects. This is only achievable through effective Space Situational Awareness (SSA) and Space Traffic Coordination (STC) systems. SSA maps out and characterizes objects in space (both satellites and debris), determining their location, trajectory and velocity, while STC actively manages the space traffic identified through SSA to prevent collisions. When a conjunction is probable, SSA/STC service providers alert the operators involved, who then decide whether to undertake a collision-avoidance maneuver.

Extending the operational life of satellites is another important aspect of debris mitigation because it reduces the need for so many new launches, thereby reducing the likelihood of more debris being created. Innovations such as electric propulsion systems that allow for greater maneuverability and extended mission durations are part of the solution, as is in-orbit servicing, maintenance and refuelling.

While these strategies focus on preventing new debris from being created, we also need effective methods for removing existing pieces of debris. This is a rapidly growing sector attracting much investment. Debris-removal technology being developed ranges from physical capture and tethered deorbit to destruction with ground and space-based laser ablation and plasma systems, as well as the emerging concept of mining debris to extract metals and gases for in-orbit processing to feed into the circular space economy.

How stakeholders are responding

The UN views space safety and space sustainability as urgent priorities. Its treaties and agreements focus on preserving the peaceful, safe, and sustainable use of outer space, preventing collisions, managing space debris, and ensuring responsible operations. Governments, space agencies and international organizations are also strengthening their focus on space sustainability.

ESA has launched its Zero Debris strategy, which is aimed at achieving a debris-neutral orbital environment by 2030. As part of this approach, ESA has updated its debris mitigation requirements and standards that will govern how its missions are designed, built, flown and disposed of. It also sets requirements for any company or institution that works with ESA on its missions.

In the U.K., the UK Space Agency is also taking a proactive role in space safety and sustainability through its Active Debris Removal (ADR) program and through the development of space sustainability standards in partnership with industry. It is also in the process of developing a space sustainability strategy to ensure a coordinated approach to sustainable practices in space.

On the other side of the pond, NASA’s Space Sustainability Strategy identifies five key challenges that are felt nationally but also within the wider space community. These include the absence of a single framework for space sustainability that has been accepted by the space community and the fact that space sustainability may be in tension with other mission interests. The strategy defines six goals that are intended to address each of the challenges alongside corresponding objectives to guide NASA’s achievements of the goals.

The U.S. is also building on the National Orbital Debris Mitigation Plan, which was released in 2022, with the Orbital Sustainability (ORBITS) Act. The Act, which has been introduced to the Senate but not yet been enacted into law, seeks to establish a program for the active remediation of orbital debris as well as requiring the development of uniform orbital debris standard practices. The Office of Space Commerce has also developed TraCSS (Traffic Coordination System for Space) to provide basic SSA data and services to civil and private space operators in support of spaceflight safety, although the system is currently in beta mode.

The International Standard Organisation (ISO) is also working on a standard for STC (Space Traffic Coordination) so that SSA activities can be standardized. Titled Space Systems — Space Traffic Coordination (STC), the standard is moving toward final publication, and its core focus is on establishing baseline protocols, data exchange formats and operational requirements for space safety, on-orbit conjunction assessment and collision avoidance.

Beyond today

While these strategies are certainly moving the industry in the right direction, there is a real need to act quickly. Success will rely not only on speed, but also on sustained and collaborative effort, as well as engagement from all space users. The decisions made and actions undertaken over the next decade will shape the space environment for generations to come.

As to whether sustainability becomes a core principle rather than an afterthought, that remains to be seen. There is, however, reason to be optimistic.

]]> <![CDATA[ Europe's Space Rider vehicle comes crashing down during drop test ]]> Europe has dropped the ball on the prototype for its first reusable spacecraft. Or, rather, the prototype itself was dropped — on purpose — but the outcome of its fall was not what engineers had hoped for.

The incident occurred during an Oct. 6 drop test of the full-scale Space Rider model, from the European Space Agency (ESA). The robotic vehicle's initial drogue parachute deployed successfully, but its main parafoil detached during deployment, leaving the prototype unable to slow its descent before crashing into the ground, according to ESA officials. The cause of the failure remains under investigation.

"Following several successful tests using representative vehicle masses, the latest system-level drop test in October was not completed as planned due to an anomaly during the parafoil deployment sequence," an ESA spokesperson confirmed in an email to Space.com. "An independent investigation is ongoing to determine its root cause and inform the next steps."

Space Rider is being developed as Europe's first reusable orbital spacecraft — an uncrewed vehicle designed to carry scientific experiments to orbit for up to two months, then return them to Earth for analysis. Its method of return, though, differs from that of any other spacecraft in operation today. Space Rider''s wingless, lifting-body design relies on a steerable parachute, or parafoil, to maneuver toward its landing area. This allows it to perform runway-style touchdowns, as opposed to other, less accurate parachute-aided recoveries in current practice.

This month's drop test was intended to demonstrate that ability, which is a critical requirement for Space Rider's planned reuse after missions in orbit, but the impact of its failure may not end up disrupting its ultimate development timeline. According to Géraldine Naja, ESA's director of space transportation, the vehicle's other remaining qualification tests aren't holding back its path to launch.

"We hope that this test will not damage, or let's say lead us to modify, the remaining schedule and qualification activities," Naja said during an ESA Council media briefing on Oct. 22. "In any case, the remaining qualification activities are not on the critical path of the development of the Space Rider."

Naja described the incident as an unfortunate but important event. "We have had many successful tests before, but testing and validation is part of the development of a space system," she said.

The lost vehicle was a full-scale test model assembled to evaluate Space Rider's descent and landing systems. The minivan-sized mockup reproduced the size and flight characteristics of its reentry module, with avionics to control its autonomous guidance and navigation systems, but the vehicle was far from a space-ready article.

The Oct. 6 test took place at a military range on the Italian island of Sardinia, where the mockup was released from a helicopter at an altitude of approximately 2 miles (3 kilometers). According to Naja, the vehicle's initial drogue parachute triggered as expected and began slowing the Space Rider mock-up's descent before its larger, steerable parafoil was supposed to unfurl. The parafoil, however, detached during deployment, leaving the vehicle in freefall before impacting the ground. ESA has subsequently recovered all the craft's components.

This month's event was the first drop test since an unsuccessful attempt in May, when a sensor flagged an issue during preparations, prompting engineers to abort the test before the model was released. Following that, Space Rider's testing range, operated by Italy's Ministry of Defense, was unavailable from June through September.

Space Rider's descent and landing qualification campaign began in 2025, with previous successes demonstrating its parafoil deployment and autonomous capabilities. Beyond its landing systems, Space Rider also underwent separate thermal protection testing earlier this year, exposing its heat-shield materials to temperatures around 2,900 degrees Fahrenheit (1,600 degrees Celsius) in plasma wind tunnel trials.

ESA has targeted Space Rider's first orbital mission for later this decade.

]]> <![CDATA[ On this day in space! Oct. 22, 1992: Ashes of 'Star Trek' creator Gene Roddenberry launch into space on NASA shuttle ]]>

On Oct. 22, 1992, the space shuttle Columbia launched into space with the ashes of Gene Roddenberry, the creator of "Star Trek," aboard.

During mission STS-52, NASA astronaut and shuttle commander James Wetherbee brought a small container with a portion of Roddenberry's ashes into space as part of his personal effects at the request of Roddenberry's widow, Majel Barrett. It was Roddenberry's lifelong dream to go to space, but he never got to go while he was alive.

But thanks to his wife, a little bit of Roddenberry finally made it to space almost exactly one year after his death. NASA and his family didn't tell anyone about it until almost two years later in 1994.

Wetherbee said he was "honored to be asked" by Barrett to carry Roddenberry's ashses on the spaceflight. "I'm just glad I was able to bring a little happiness to the family," he said, according to Newsweek.

Here's why it mattered

The launch of Roddenberry's ashes into space on NASA's STS-52 mission aboard the space shuttle Columbia marked the world's first "space burial," but it wouldn't be the last.

About five years after Roddenberry's memorial flight, in 1997, the space memorial company Celestis began launching a series of "burial" flights by flying capsules with human cremains on rockets . In fact, more of Roddenberry's ashes flew on Celestis' "founders flight" in April 1997 aboard an air-launched Pegasus rocket that took off from the Canary Islands in Spain. The ashes of Roddenberry's wife and of Star Trek actor James Doohan have also flown in space, among others.

Celestis has gone on to launch human cremains on many suborbital and orbital flights, including some on SpaceX Falcon 9 rockets. The company even launched the ashes of the late astronomer Eugene Shoemaker to the moon in 1999 on the Luna 1 flight, with another set of cremains launched into deep space on the Enterprise mission in 2023.

About five years after Roddenberry's memorial flight, in 1997, the space memorial company Celestis began launching a series of "burial" flights by flying capsules with human cremains on rockets . In fact, more of Roddenberry's ashes flew on Celestis' "founders flight" in April 1997 aboard an air-launched Pegasus rocket that took off from the Canary Islands in Spain. The ashes of Roddenberry's wife and of Star Trek actor James Doohan have also flown in space, among others.

Celestis has gone on to launch human cremains on many suborbital and orbital flights, including some on SpaceX Falcon 9 rockets. ]]> <![CDATA[ After Starshield interruption, Ukraine wants to build its own satellite communication network with ICEYE and Nokia ]]> Ukraine wants its own satellite-communication system, which shouldn't be surprising given the events of the past week or so.

The Ukrainian military just signed a letter of intent with two Finnish companies — the telecom giant Nokia and satellite maker ICEYE — to look into developing a sovereign satellite-communications network for Ukraine.

"Ukraine needs secure, sovereign and high-performance satellite communications systems that it controls," ICEYE cofounder and CEO Rafal Modrzewski said in a statement today (Oct. 22). "We have a proven track record of delivering sovereign missions at speed to help build that capability. ICEYE has proudly supported Ukraine since 2022, and we remain committed to continuing that support today."

Ukraine relies heavily on satellite-based communications and data to defend itself from Russia, which invaded the nation in February 2022 and continues to attack it with ground troops, missiles and drone strikes.

But Ukraine does not own those satellites. It primarily uses the services provided by SpaceX's Starlink megaconstellation in low Earth orbit (LEO) and Starshield, a military-grade, jamming-resistant version of Starlink employed by the U.S. government and its allies.

Starshield in particular is crucial to Ukraine, as it allows the nation to operate fast-moving drones over large distances in war zones. Ukraine has gotten very good at drone warfare, employing these little robots both in offensive and defensive capacities.

On Oct. 14, however, Ukrainian soldiers and officials reported a severe throttling of their access to Starshield services — a speed limit on terminal-carrying drones, which caused many of them to fall out of the sky.

It's not entirely clear who's behind the throttling. Some U.S. officials have apparently said the order came from Elon Musk, but the billionaire SpaceX founder and CEO put the ultimate responsibility on the Trump administration.

"Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS," Musk said on Oct. 14 via X, the social media platform he owns.

Whoever made the call, it certainly wasn't Ukraine. And the Starshield throttling — which apparently is still in effect — has doubtless reinforced the nation's desire to control its own satellite-communications infrastructure.

"Nations need communications they can rely on in every situation. Satellite networks extend and protect connectivity when networks on the ground are disrupted," Mikko Hautala, Nokia's chief geopolitical and government relations officer and chairman of Nokia Defense, said in the same statement.

"This makes them a key part of any secure communications system," he added. "Through this Letter of Intent, together with Ukraine and ICEYE, we will explore how trusted, sovereign satellite communications can strengthen Ukraine's resilience and give it control over the connectivity it depends on."

Nokia and ICEYE announced on Oct. 1 that they plan to work together to help nations develop such sovereign satcom systems. The partnership with Ukraine follows on from that earlier agreement.

ICEYE has already been aiding the Ukrainian defense effort. The Finnish company and its U.S. subsidiary jointly operate a fleet of Earth-observing satellites in LEO, which study our planet using synthetic aperture radar. Ukraine uses data from the ICEYE constellation for intelligence and planning purposes.

This relationship has put ICEYE — or one of its satellites, at least — in Russia's crosshairs. A Russian inspector satellite called Kosmos 2612 recently made an extremely close approach to ICEYE-X36, which is operated by ICEYE US.

The goal of the unsanctioned rendezvous is unclear. Russia may have wanted to assess the satellite's capabilities or interfere with it in some way. Or perhaps the nation simply wanted to send a message, letting ICEYE (and Ukraine) know that it could mess with satellites if it wanted to.

]]> <![CDATA[ The 2027 total solar eclipse will plunge these 10 ancient Egyptian temples and monuments into darkness ]]> The total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027, has an ancient feel. It will certainly be a celestial event for the ages — at 6 minutes 23 seconds, it will feature the longest totality on land of the 21st century and the longest anywhere until 2114. However, its point of greatest eclipse occurs just a few miles from Thebes, the magnificent religious and political capital of ancient Egypt's Middle Kingdom and New Kingdom.

On the east bank of the mighty Nile is Luxor, the great city of the living, with its massive temple complexes of Karnak and Luxor. On its west bank is the city of the dead, which includes the Valley of the Kings and the Temple of Hatshepsut. Modern Luxor, population 285,000, is set to become a focal point for eclipse chasers on Aug. 2, 2027, and will attract many thousands of international visitors. They'll come for the forecasted 0% chance of clouds and the era-defining duration of totality, but also to tour ancient Egypt's temples and monuments.

The chances of actually witnessing totality at any of the major temples are probably slim. Still, almost every eclipse chaser headed to Luxor will want to tour them before or after the eclipse. Visitors should be prepared for extreme August heat and check official opening and access arrangements before planning to watch the eclipse at any archaeological site. Certified eclipse glasses are essential during the partial phases; only during totality, when the sun is completely covered, is it safe to look without them.

Ancient monuments in the path of totality

Not all of ancient Egypt will experience totality. Egypt's top-ranking monument, the Pyramids at Giza, near Cairo, lies north of the path of totality and will get a 95% partial solar eclipse. Abu Simbel, on the shores of Lake Nasser south of Aswan, will also see a 92% partial solar eclipse. No matter, Luxor is home to some of the world's most impressive and well-preserved ancient monuments. Here are its temples, necropolises and palaces — and those nearby, also in the 160-mile (257-kilometer)-wide path of totality — that will have the moon's umbral shadow fall upon them on Aug. 2, 2027. All times, totality durations and historical cloud cover data come from Time and Date.

1. Karnak Temple

Location: East bank of Luxor, Egypt

Start of totality and duration: 1:02 p.m. EEST; 6 minutes, 19 seconds

Historical cloud cover: 0%

Dedicated to the god Amun-Ra — a fusion of the hidden god of the sun Amun and the ancient sun god Ra — this vast temple complex will be the hottest ticket in town for the eclipse. One of Egypt's most impressive and well-preserved ancient monuments, it's a place designed by ancient astronomers — the winter solstice sunrise still illuminates the innermost sanctuary. Access arrangements for eclipse day have yet to be confirmed, so keep an eye on official announcements before making plans to watch totality from the complex.

2. Luxor Temple

Location: East bank of Luxor, Egypt

Start of totality and duration: 1:02 p.m. EEST; 6 minutes, 19 seconds

Historical cloud cover: 0%

This is one of Egypt's best-preserved ancient temples and a must-see during the 2027 eclipse. It's on the banks of the Nile near the city center, so it's relatively easy to visit. Dedicated to the god Amun, it is known for its beautiful pillars and intricate carvings. A 75-foot (23 meters) tall obelisk on the east side of its entrance will point at the eclipsed sun almost directly overhead on Aug. 2, 2027. Its missing right-hand obelisk is in the Place de la Concorde, Paris.

3. Valley of the Kings

Location: West Bank of Luxor, Egypt

Start of totality and duration: 1:01 p.m. EEST; 6 minutes, 19 seconds

Historical cloud cover: 0%

This incredible necropolis is home to the tombs of the pharaohs and is a testament to the advanced engineering and architectural skills of the ancient Egyptians. Of course, you don't want to be underground for totality, but some of the tombs are a must-see. Your tickets include entry to any three tombs of your choice from those open that day, with extra tickets available for the really impressive ones—the spectacular KV17 (Seti I), small but iconic KV62 (Tutankhamun), and KV9 (Ramesses V & VI). The latter's Corridor G has a ceiling decoration that may depict a deep partial solar eclipse from 1143 BC.

4. Mortuary Temple of Hatshepsut

Location: West Bank of Luxor, Egypt

Start of totality and duration: 1:01 p.m. EEST; 6 minutes, 19 seconds

Historical cloud cover: 0%

If one temple is best suited to crowds for an eclipse, it's this vast, open-air gem dedicated to the legendary queen who became pharaoh. However, with almost no shade, it could be the least practical option. Three huge terraces rise above the desert floor and into the cliffs of Deir el-Bahari to the west. It's an absolute masterpiece.

5. Colossi of Memnon

Location: West Bank of Luxor, Egypt

Start of totality and duration: 1:01 p.m. EEST; 6 minutes, 19 seconds

Historical cloud cover: 0%

This is where we get to temples that are fairly well known, but likely won't have as much pressure on them from eclipse chasers as the big three — Karnak, Luxor and Hatshepsut. However, anyone looking for ways to get temple architecture into images of an eclipse at zenith should look no further than these two large stone statues of Pharaoh Amenhotep III. Behind them are the ruins of the largest temple in the Theban Necropolis.

6. Medinet Habu

Location: West Bank of Luxor, Egypt

Start of totality and duration: 1:01 p.m. EEST; 6 minutes, 19 seconds

Chance of clouds: 0%

Getting off the beaten track in August 2027 will be near-impossible, but here's an option — the Mortuary Temple of Ramesses III. Featuring towering stone columns, colorful reliefs (despite being 3,200 years old) and famous carvings, it's bypassed by tour buses heading straight for Hatshepsut.

7. Ramesseum

Location: West Bank of Luxor, Egypt

Start of totality and duration: 1:01 p.m. EEST; 6 minutes, 19 seconds

Historical cloud cover: 0%

Another temple that, without Karnak and Luxor nearby, would be rammed with visitors, is the Ramesseum — the mortuary temple of Ramesses II. Featuring the remains of a huge fallen statue that inspired Shelley's poem Ozymandias, it's in an area once used by the artisans who built the royal tombs, and slightly off the tourist route.

8. Temple of Khnum

Location: Esna, Egypt

Start of totality and duration: 1:02 p.m. EEST; 5 minutes, 47 seconds

Historical cloud cover: 0%

If you want to avoid the scrum of eclipse chasers in Luxor on and around Aug. 2, the Temple of Khnum could be an option. Located in Esna, about 34 miles (55 kilometers) south of Luxor, the so-called 'Rainbow Temple' (for its colorful ceilings) is dedicated to the ram-headed creator god Khnum. Dating from the Greco-Roman era, there's a vast Hypostyle Hall that sits below modern street level, which could be good for some shade.

9. Temple of Dendera

Location: Qena, Egypt

Start of totality and duration: 1:01 p.m. EEST; 6 minutes, 15 seconds

Historical cloud cover: 0%

If you want to escape Luxor but (almost) keep its long totality, head to Qena, 40 miles (65 km) north, where one of Egypt's best-preserved and most beautiful temples stands. Dendera was the cult center for Hathor, one of the most important and popular deities in ancient Egypt and known as the 'lady of the sky.' The temple's entrance has six massive columns, each decorated with Hathor's head, and its ceiling features astronomical engravings.

10. Temple of Horus

Location: Edfu, Egypt

Start of totality and duration: 1:04 p.m. EEST; 5 minutes, 20 seconds

Historical cloud cover: 0%

Another great option for those who prioritize ancient Egyptian surroundings over the longest possible totality is the Temple of Horus, one of the most striking and best-preserved temples in ancient Egypt. About 68 miles (110 km) south of Luxor, it's dedicated to the sun and sky god Horus, one of the main gods in ancient Egypt, whose right eye represents the sun and left eye the moon. The temple's stone roofs are intact, so its Hypostyle Halls, inner chambers and central sanctuary provide some shade.

]]> <![CDATA[ Van Gogh's 'The Starry Night' depicts the sky on July 22, 1889, researchers find ]]> Researchers think they might have pinpointed the exact night sky that we see depicted in Vincent van Gogh's iconic painting "The Starry Night."

Perhaps one of the most famous paintings in modern history, Van Gogh's "The Starry Night" carries a legacy that continues to inspire and mystify generation after generation. But while you might see in its swirls of color and bright spots of starlight a night sky derived purely from imagination, some scientists think it represents an actual view — one that includes a waning crescent moon, Venus and the Hyades cluster. And they may know exactly when this sky appeared..

In a new study, researchers suggest that "The Starry Night" depicts the pre-dawn sky seen around July 22, 1889 from Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, where Van Gogh painted it. But while this sky happens to perfectly match the one depicted in the artwork, art historians have long thought that Van Gogh painted this piece in June. Could these findings shift the date of this legendary artwork?

Finding a painted sky

This investigation started decades ago with art historian Albert Boime and astronomer George Abell at UCLA in 1984 and continued in the following years with astronomer Charles Whitney at Harvard University. However, these earlier analyses did not agree with one another, and there was no true consensus about exactly when the sky matched with the painting.

So the question remained, lingering in the minds of those with a shared love for both art and space. And a team led by Elijah Jeong-hyun Kim, the CEO of South Korean robotic telescope company SLLAB and a Ph.D. candidate at Kyung Hee University's School of Space Research, picked up the search once more.

"When they see a fragment of a starry sky, observational astronomers like me and amateur astronomers alike will want to solve the puzzle. I am simply someone who pursued that process a little more actively," Kim told Space.com.

But how did Kim's team come to their conclusion, after others had failed to nail down a date over the decades? In short, "we analyzed the painting astronomically, analyzed documents about his situation in July 1889, and then carried out ecological and meteorological investigations," Kim said.

To start with, the team analyzed the sky from the exact location in Saint-Rémy where Van Gogh is said to have painted "The Starry Night." They then used observational geometry to map the historical night sky.

"Modern telescopes are equipped with a function called astrometry, which compares an image of the night sky with celestial coordinates stored in a computer and automatically extracts the coordinates of the image," Kim said. "We used Procrustes analysis, a method that compares only the 'shape' of two sets of points. After matching their position, size and rotation, it measures how similar the two shapes are from the differences that remain (the residuals)."

"Because a star cluster on the canvas may be larger or smaller than in reality and slightly tilted, this method was the right fit. It allowed us to explain, in quantitative terms, what earlier studies had described only qualitatively as 'resembling a certain constellation,'" Kim added.

But this quantitative analysis wasn't enough to say for sure that this was the right-fitting sky, as different constellations could fit to a similar degree, Kim explained. To get closer to their answer, the team combined their analysis with a deep dive through history.

"We also checked whether the stars were actually in that part of the pre-dawn sky on that date, whether they fall within the painter’s field of view, and whether the appearance of the moon and Venus matches the painting. It was the Hyades that satisfied all of these conditions," Kim said.

Exploring astro-art history

As mentioned, the date of this matching sky comes in late July, a month after art historians think Van Gogh painted "The Starry Night." But the researchers suggest that their findings could provide evidence to support the idea that the work was actually painted in July.

Letters written by Van Gogh as early as 1888 describe his desire to paint a star-filled sky. A letter dated April 12, 1888 reads: "A starry sky, for example, well — it’s a thing that I’d like to try to do, just as in the daytime I’ll try to paint a green meadow studded with dandelions."

Kim followed these letters through the months to try and find more information that could potentially alleviate the discrepancy between the matching skies and the actual month the painting was created. Kim pointed to a letter from between late May and early June 1889 that reads: "This morning I saw the countryside from my window a long time before sunrise with nothing but the morning star, which looked very big."

Kim drew on "personal imagination" to find ties between Van Gogh's sky observations in these months and what they might mean for the painting's timeline, Kim shared, so this doesn't definitively change the view of this painting's history. However, Kim suggested that these records could indicate that Van Gogh was repeatedly looking up and watching the pre-dawn sky, which could have led to him seeing this exact sky on July 22.

The painting itself even ignites uncertainty among art historians. As the researchers cite in their new paper, leading art historians see "The Starry Night" as stylistically different from Van Gogh's other works during the month of June, drawing further questions over the date painted.

"What our study shows is that the sky in the painting matches, in both observation and shape, the real pre-dawn sky around July 22. So, what we propose is the possibility that Vincent conceived the idea in June and completed the painting after July 22," Kim said.

However, "I think further research in art history and conservation science could shed more light on this question," Kim added.

This work was described in a study published Oct. 22 in the journal Scientific Reports.

So the question remained, lingering in the minds of those with a shared love for both art and space. And a team led by Elijah Jeong-hyun Kim, the CEO of South Korean robotic telescope company SLLAB and a Ph.D. candidate at Kyung Hee University's School of Space Research, picked up the search once more.

"When they see a fragment of a starry sky, observational astronomers like me and amateur astronomers alike will want to solve the puzzle. I am simply someone who pursued that process a little more actively," Kim told Space.com.

But how did Kim's team come to their conclusion, after others had failed to nail down a date over the decades? In short, "we analyzed the painting astronomically, analyzed documents about his situation in July 1889, and then carried out ecological and meteorological investigations," Kim said.

To start with, the team analyzed the sky from the exact location in Saint-Rémy where Van Gogh is said to have painted "The Starry Night." They then used observational geometry to map the historical night sky.

"Modern telescopes are equipped with a function called astrometry, which compares an image of the night sky with celestial coordinates stored in a computer and automatically extracts the coordinates of the image," Kim said. "We used Procrustes analysis, a method that compares only the 'shape' of two sets of points. After matching their position, size and rotation, it measures how similar the two shapes are from the differences that remain (the residuals)."

"Because a star cluster on the canvas may be larger or smaller than in reality and slightly tilted, this method was the right fit. It allowed us to explain, in quantitative terms, what earlier studies had described only qualitatively as 'resembling a certain constellation,'" Kim added.

But this quantitative analysis wasn't enough to say for sure that this was the right-fitting sky, as different constellations could fit to a similar degree, Kim explained. To get closer to their answer, the team combined their analysis with a deep dive through history.

"We also checked whether the stars were actually in that part of the pre-dawn sky on that date, whether they fall within the painter’s field of view, and whether the appearance of the moon and Venus matches the painting. It was the Hyades that satisfied all of these conditions," Kim said.

Exploring astro-art history

As mentioned, the date of this matching sky comes in late July, a month after art historians think Van Gogh painted "The Starry Night." But the researchers suggest that their findings could provide evidence to support the idea that the work was actually painted in July.

Letters written by Van Gogh as early as 1888 describe his desire to paint a star-filled sky. A letter dated April 12, 1888 reads: "A starry sky, for example, well — it’s a thing that I’d like to try to do, just as in the daytime I’ll try to paint a green meadow studded with dandelions."

Kim followed these letters through the months to try and find more information that could potentially alleviate the discrepancy between the matching skies and the actual month the painting was created. Kim pointed to a letter from between late May and early June 1889 that reads: "This morning I saw the countryside from my window a long time before sunrise with nothing but the morning star, which looked very big."

Kim drew on "personal imagination" to find ties between Van Gogh's sky observations in these months and what they might mean for the painting's timeline, Kim shared, so this doesn't definitively change the view of this painting's history. However, Kim suggested that these records could indicate that Van Gogh was repeatedly looking up and watching the pre-dawn sky, which could have led to him seeing this exact sky on July 22.

The painting itself even ignites uncertainty among art historians. As the researchers cite in their new paper, leading art historians see "The Starry Night" as stylistically different from Van Gogh's other works during the month of June, drawing further questions over the date painted.

"What our study shows is that the sky in the painting matches, in both observation and shape, the real pre-dawn sky around July 22. So, what we propose is the possibility that Vincent conceived the idea in June and completed the painting after July 22," Kim said.

However, "I think further research in art history and conservation science could shed more light on this question," Kim added.

This work was described in a study published Oct. 22 in the journal Scientific Reports.

 <description>Krajský soud v Olomouci uložil v pátek Jiřímu Kudličkovi za otravy kolegů ve šternberské zbrojovce 24 let vězení a zabezpečovací detenci.   <item>
   <title>Vánoční strom pro Václavák našli na Českolipsku. Smrk má 21 metrů</title>
   <link>https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/zpravy-region/vanocni-strom-pro-vaclavak-nasli-na-ceskolipsku-smrk-ma-21-metru/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=zpravy-region</link>
   <description>Z Lužických hor až do samotného centra Prahy. Vánoční strom, který letos ozdobí Václavské náměstí, vyrostl v Rousínově na Českolipsku. Smrk měří přibližně 21 metrů a obvod jeho kmene dosahuje téměř dvou metrů. </description>

   <description>Aplikace Můj Albert zůstává po kybernetickém incidentu v mateřské skupině Ahold Delhaize mimo provoz. Společnost potvrdila, že za incidentem stojí škodlivé jednání třetí strany. Zákazníci mohou v obchodech dál nakupovat a využívat vybrané slevy i bez aplikace. </description>

  <item>
   <title>Průkopník, poslanec i fotograf. Odešel dlouholetý primář českolipské interny</title>
   <link>https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/zpravy-region/cerbak-primar-interna-ceska-lipa-nemocnice-zemrel-vzpominka-gut/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=zpravy-region</link>
   <description>S podzimem skončila dlouhá a medicínsky bohatá životní pouť lékaře Miroslava Čerbáka, který odešel 18. října 2026 ve svých 90 letech v domku v Dolní Řasnici u Frýdlantu. Tam se přestěhovali s manželkou Hanou před lety po ukončení svého velmi aktivního medicínského nasazení v českolipské nemocnici, se kterou spojili prakticky celý lékařský život po ukončení studia. Na svého kolegu vzpomíná primář českolipské pediatrie Josef Gut.</description>
   <pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 10:22:38 +0200</pubDate>
   <guid>https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/zpravy-region/cerbak-primar-interna-ceska-lipa-nemocnice-zemrel-vzpominka-gut/</guid>
   <category>Českolipsko </category>
   <enclosure url="https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/images/api/image/1366x768/e29/e29489d7-c4cf-4f4b-a2a4-7fec524e0ca5.jpeg" length="0" type="image/jpeg"/>
   <media:content url="https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/images/api/image/1366x768/e29/e29489d7-c4cf-4f4b-a2a4-7fec524e0ca5.jpeg" medium="image" height="768" width="1366">
    <media:description>Miroslav Čerbák miloval fotografování, portrétoval čápy, hlavně v Jablonném v Podještědí, nebo alejová stromořadí podél silnic na Frýdlantsku.</media:description>
    <media:credit>archiv Josefa Guta</media:credit>

    <item>
      <title>Pumový poplach na ukrajinské ambasádě ve Washingtonu. Uzavřeli i přilehlý most</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni/ukrajinska-ambasada-washington-predmet-evakuace-poplach.A261023_173110_zahranicni_fohl#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Ve Washingtonu byl poblíž ukrajinského velvyslanectví nalezen podezřelý předmět. Americká tajná služba byla proto nucena budovu ihned evakuovat a uzavřít nedaleký most Key Bridge. Úřady později zjistily, že se nejednalo o hrozbu.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Na poslední pivo či koleno. Legendární hospoda U Jarolímků dnes zavírá</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/praha/zpravy/hospoda-u-jarolimku-konci-praha-liben-posledni-pivo.A261023_175411_praha-zpravy_epkbn#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Ještě na posledních pár piv nebo hospodskou klasiku na talíři v podobě vepřového kolene či hovězího tataráku dneska lidé míří do legendární libeňské hospody U Jarolímků. Mnoha místním je líto, že podnik mizí. „Bohužel to dopadlo tak, jak to dopadnout nemělo,“ smutní před dveřmi muž, který se sem dlouho chystal. „Byla tady dobrá atmosféra a na okolní poměry byla levná,“ hodnotí další, který k Jarolímkům chodívá roky. Nyní zdejší podnik nahradí nový bytový dům.</description>
      <pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 16:22:00 GMT</pubDate>
      <category domain="https://www.idnes.cz/praha/zpravy">Praha - Praha - zprávy</category>

    <item>
      <title>Prudká hádka kvůli poplatkům ČT. Snažíte se ukrást zemi, vyčetl koalici Skopeček</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/koalice-prosadila-prednostni-jednani-o-konci-poplatku-pro-ct-i-rozhlas.A261023_095639_domaci_kop#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Ve Sněmovně se strhla prudká hádka při projednávání vládního návrhu zrušit televizní a rozhlasové poplatky. Koalice ANO, SPD a Motoristů sobě se rozhodla neumožnit přestávky poslaneckým klubům opozičních stran. „Je to poprvé, kdy se hlasovalo o přestávkách, nikdy se to nestalo,“ rozčiloval se šéf poslanců ODS Marek Benda. 
</description>

    <item>
      <title>Média nedáme, skandovali lidé před Sněmovnou. Poslance ANO vypískali</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/domaci/media-sluzba-poslanecka-snemovna-demostrace-klempir-vlada.A261023_133413_domaci_sahu#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Zhruba tři sta lidí se v pátek narychlo sešlo před Poslaneckou sněmovnou na protest proti koaličnímu záměru zrušit koncesionářské poplatky pro Českou televizi a Český rozhlas. Z megafonů znělo skandování „Média nedáme!“, přítomní tleskali vyhlášení plánované stávky v obou médiích a poslance hnutí ANO Denise Doksanského při příchodu do budovy vypískali.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Naděje pro hladovějící. Melania Trumpová vyjednala příměří pro ukrajinské Olešky</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni/melania-trumpova-bileho-domu-primiri-olesky-rusko-ukrajina.A261023_154358_zahranicni_dtt#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Manželka amerického prezidenta Melania Trumpová zprostředkovala podle vyjádření Bílého domu dohodu o dočasném příměří mezi Ruskem a Ukrajinou u města Olešky. <title>EU se snaží zmírnit nedávno zavedená obalová pravidla, která potápí malé e-shopy. Rada a Parlament se ale neshodnou, jak na to</title>
<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/eu-se-snazi-zmirnit-nedavno-zavedena-obalova-pravidla-ktera-potapi-male-e-shopy-rada-a-parlament-se-ale-neshodnou-jak-na-to/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Povinnost, která malým e-shopům komplikuje prodej do dal&#353;ích zemí EU, by se mohla pro malé e-shopy zmírnit. Evropský parlament i Rada EU chtějí pozastavit pravidlo, podle něhož musí firmy jmenovat zástupce pro roz&#353;ířenou odpovědnost výrobce v jednotlivých zemích, kam dodávají zboží v obalech. Neshodují se ale na tom, koho by se výjimka měla týkat.</description>

 <description>Jared Kushner, zeť a velvyslanec Donalda Trumpa, popřel obvinění Vanity Fair, podle něhož nizozemská zpravodajská služba při sledování aktivit na jeho telefonu odhalila finanční transakce, do kterých byly zapojeny vlády z Blízkého východu. „Nevíme, do jaké míry hraje roli zájem USA a kdy záměr Trumpovy rodiny,“ říká pro Radiožurnál David Mareček, amerikanista z Katedry mezinárodních vztahů a evropských studií Metropolitní univerzity Praha.</description>

 <description>Izraelský premiér Benjamin Netanjahu v pátek po střelbě u Hebronu prohlásil, že zvažuje na Západním břehu Jordánu největší vojenskou operaci od roku 1967. Napsala to izraelská média a agentura AFP. Podle Netanjahua je armáda připravena příkazy vykonat. Oznámení přichází několik dní před parlamentními volbami, v nichž bude šéf izraelského kabinetu usilovat o znovuzvolení.</description>

<item>
 <title>Nejméně jednoho mrtvého si vyžádala střelba na předměstí Paříže. Policie pachatele zadržela</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/nejmene-jednoho-mrtveho-si-vyzadala-strelba-na-predmesti-parize-policie_2610231245_vsn</link>
 <description>Nejméně jednoho mrtvého si v pátek dopoledne vyžádala střelba na předměstí Paříže. Informoval o tom podle agentury AFP policejní zdroj, podle něhož muž střílel na ulici. Informaci poté potvrdil i francouzský premiér Sébastien Lecornu. Další čtyři lidé utrpěli zranění. Podle úřadů jsou na místě záchranné složky a počet obětí zatím není definitivní.</description>

 <description>Rumunští záchranáři pátrají po námořnících ze zasažené nákladní lodi poblíž rumunských břehů v Černém moři. Jeden člen většinově ukrajinské posádky zemřel, tři se pohřešují, devět se podařilo zachránit, píší média s odvoláním na rumunský námořní úřad.  <description>Rakouské ministerstvo zahraničí v pátek oznámilo, že vyhošťuje čtyři ruské diplomaty. Dopustili se podle něho jednání, které je v rozporu s jejich diplomatickým statusem. Tři diplomaté působili na ruské ambasádě, jeden v ruské delegaci pro vojenskou bezpečnost a kontrolu zbrojení při Organizaci pro bezpečnost a spolupráci v Evropě (OBSE), informuje agentura APA.  <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/vucic-nebo-studenti-v-srbsku-skoncila-kampan-pred-volbami-realnou-sanci-na_2610231038_vsn</link>
 <description>Ve volbách půjde o boj dvou nejsilnějších politických formací. Roky vládnoucí koalice Sjednocené Srbsko exprezidenta Aleksandra Vučiće a opozičního hnutí s názvem Studenti vítězí. To vzešlo z dvouletých protikorupčních protestů v Bělehradě.
</description>

 <description>Prezident Petr Pavel patří mezi pět politiků, o nichž evropští lídři uvažují jako o hlavním vyjednavači s ruským vládcem Vladimirem Putinem o ukončení války na Ukrajině.  <description>Tisíce lidí narozených v Jižní Koreji, kteří byli adoptováni do Spojených států, zjišťují, že jejich adopce mohly být založeny na podvodných dokumentech nebo se uskutečnit bez souhlasu biologických rodičů. Někteří z nich také popisují zkušenosti s týráním v adoptivních rodinách a zařízeních pro děti. Jižní Korea loni uznala odpovědnost státu za to, že umožnil rozsáhlé posílání dětí do zahraničí k adopci, napsal deník The Guardian.</description>

 <description>Šéf společnosti SpaceX Elon Musk obnovil Ukrajině přístup k satelitní síti Starlink, prohlásil ve čtvrtek večer podle tiskových agentur americký prezident Donald Trump. Odmítl však říci, zda s Muskem o věci přímo hovořil. Kyjev si v posledních dnech stěžoval na omezení rychlosti připojení k systému, na kterém je ukrajinská armáda závislá při obraně proti ruské agresi a který využívá ke komunikaci na bojišti i k provozu dronů.</description>

<title>Zatímco se řešily chyby v PHP, útočníci propašovali malware do oblíbené open-source knihovny</title>
<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/zatimco-se-resily-chyby-v-php-utocnici-propasovali-malware-do-oblibene-open-source-knihovny/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Během dění kolem kritické zranitelnosti v PHP se útočníci pokusili zneužít dal&#353;í roz&#353;ířený nástroj, upozorňuje kyberbezpečnostní startup Aisle, který založili Ondřej Vlček, Stanislav Fort a Jaya Ballo. Podle firmy se podařilo dostat &#353;kodlivý kód do nové verze knihovny LiteLLM pro Python, kterou vývojáři používají při práci s modely umělé inteligence a která má přes 20 milionů stažení týdně. Malware měl krást přístupové údaje a umožnit útočníkům vzdáleně spou&#353;tět vlastní příkazy. Napadení potvrdili i tvůrci Lite LLM, kteří zveřejnili také dal&#353;í podrobnosti.</description>

<rss version="2.0" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><title>Liberecká Drbna</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz</link><description>Liberecká Drbna</description><language>cs</language><item><title>Zahrada se chystá na zimu. Co ještě v říjnu stihnout, než udeří mrazy?</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903806-zahrada-se-chysta-na-zimu-co-jeste-v-rijnu-stihnout-nez-uderi-mrazy.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903806-zahrada-se-chysta-na-zimu-co-jeste-v-rijnu-stihnout-nez-uderi-mrazy.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 18:01:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Helena Révay</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Sklizeň poslední zeleniny, výsadba česneku i jarních květin nebo péče o trávník. Říjen na zahradě rozhodně neznamená konec práce. Některé úkoly se přitom vyplatí neodkládat, protože první mrazíky mohou změnit plány.</description></item><item><title>Pocty hejtmana získalo 10 osobností, Jizerská 50 i dvanáctiletá zachránkyně</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903801-pocty-hejtmana-ziskalo-10-osobnosti-jizerska-50-i-dvanactileta-zachrankyne.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903801-pocty-hejtmana-ziskalo-10-osobnosti-jizerska-50-i-dvanactileta-zachrankyne.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 17:00:00 +0200</pubDate><category>Společnost</category><description>Deset osobností a poprvé v historii i sportovní akce – slavný závod Jizerská 50 – obdržely Poctu hejtmana Libereckého kraje 2026. Zvláštní poděkování a ocenění sv. Zdislavy získala dvanáctiletá Tereza Sasková za záchranu života. Slavnostní večer byl poslední udílením poct pro hejtmana Martina Půtu.</description></item><item><title>Hledal prý houby, našel spravedlnost: Zloděj se 100 tisíci z pošty skončil ve vazbě</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/903865-hledal-pry-houby-nasel-spravedlnost-zlodej-se-100-tisici-z-posty-skoncil-ve-vazbe.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/903865-hledal-pry-houby-nasel-spravedlnost-zlodej-se-100-tisici-z-posty-skoncil-ve-vazbe.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 15:20:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>Rychle nabyl, ještě rychleji pozbyl. Ostřílený recidivista ukradl na Liberecku z pošty přes 100 tisíc korun. Blesková intuice dopravních policistů ho ale okamžitě dohledala u herny. Muž pod vlivem drog se marně vymlouval na houbaření. Plný batoh peněz zabavili policisté, muž skončil ve vazbě.</description></item><item><title>Online registrace na Sokolský běh republiky končí už 25. října</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/sport/903699-online-registrace-na-sokolsky-beh-republiky-konci-uz-25-rijna.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/sport/903699-online-registrace-na-sokolsky-beh-republiky-konci-uz-25-rijna.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 14:01:00 +0200</pubDate><category>Sport</category><description>Osmý ročník Sokolského běhu republiky je za dveřmi. Tradiční běžecká oslava vzniku Československa propojí už ve středu 28. října více než 90 lokalit v Česku i zahraničí. Pokud chcete být u toho, zbystřete. Online registrace končí již tuto neděli 25. října.</description></item><item><title>Víkend bude chladnější, přes den bude kolem 11 stupňů, na horách může sněžit</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903817-vikend-bude-chladnejsi-pres-den-bude-kolem-11-stupnu-na-horach-muze-snezit.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903817-vikend-bude-chladnejsi-pres-den-bude-kolem-11-stupnu-na-horach-muze-snezit.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 12:45:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Víkend bude v Česku spíše chladnější, denní teploty se budou pohybovat kolem 11 stupňů Celsia. V neděli se zatáhne a na většině území bude pršet. Na horách může sněžit. Vyplývá to z předpovědi Českého hydrometeorologického ústavu (ČHMÚ).</description></item><item><title>Slovan o víkendu nehraje. V týmu Baníku řádí nemoc</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/903850-slovan-o-vikendu-nehraje-v-tymu-baniku-radi-nemoc.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/903850-slovan-o-vikendu-nehraje-v-tymu-baniku-radi-nemoc.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 11:43:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Fotbal</category><description>Liberečtí fotbalisté mají o víkendu neplánované volno. Jejich zápas se odkládá z důvodu infekčního onemocnění v týmu Baníku Ostrava. Kdy se bude hrát, to jisté není, o náhradním termínu ještě nebylo rozhodnuto.</description></item><item><title>Strašidelná zoo a koutek v Liberci: pátek a sobota plné masek, bubeníků a kouzel</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903798-strasidelna-zoo-a-koutek-v-liberci-patek-a-sobota-plne-masek-bubeniku-a-kouzel.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903798-strasidelna-zoo-a-koutek-v-liberci-patek-a-sobota-plne-masek-bubeniku-a-kouzel.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 10:59:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Bojíte se rádi? Dnes a zítra, 23. a 24. října, ovládne Liberec strašidelná zábava v zoo i dětském koutku. Těšit se můžete na večerní stezku, zónu pro obzvlášť otrlé, bubenickou show, ohňové představení a v sobotu i na kouzelníka. Vstupenky platí běžné, do koutku se platí zvlášť.</description></item><item><title>Dnešek má být nejrizikovějším dnem na silnicích. Pozor hlavně odpoledne</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/903766-dnesek-ma-byt-nejrizikovejsim-dnem-na-silnicich-pozor-hlavne-odpoledne.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/903766-dnesek-ma-byt-nejrizikovejsim-dnem-na-silnicich-pozor-hlavne-odpoledne.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 08:53:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Markéta Hamerníková</dc:creator><category>Doprava</category><description>Pátek 23. října vychází podle analýzy dlouhodobých statistik jako nejrizikovější den letošního roku na českých silnicích. Potkává se v něm silný páteční provoz s podzimními riziky. Řidiči by měli dávat pozor hlavně v odpolední špičce mezi 14. a 17. hodinou.</description></item><item><title>Policisté pátrají po pohřešovaném muži z Liberecka. Neviděli jste ho?</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/903797-policiste-patraji-po-pohresovanem-muzi-z-liberecka-rodina-se-o-nej-boji.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/903797-policiste-patraji-po-pohresovanem-muzi-z-liberecka-rodina-se-o-nej-boji.html</guid><pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 06:30:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>Po 34letém Lukáši Mudrém z Liberecka pátrají od včerejšího dne policisté. Muž je vysoký zhruba 175 cm, má plavé vlnité vlasy, šedomodré oči a vousy, tzv. kotlety. Jakékoliv informace o jeho pohybu či výskytu přijmou policisté na kterékoli služebně nebo na tísňové lince 158. Rodina má o něj strach.</description></item><item><title>Skvělý výsledek Jablonce. S Brightonem uhrál remízu</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/903787-skvely-vysledek-jablonce-s-brightonem-uhral-remizu.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/903787-skvely-vysledek-jablonce-s-brightonem-uhral-remizu.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 22 Oct 2026 20:47:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Fotbal</category><description>Jablonečtí fotbalisté se ve druhém zápase v základní skupiny Konferenční ligy postavili anglickému Brightonu. Ten má nyní skvělou formu a ničí jednoho soupeře za druhým. Na severu Čech to ale nepotvrdil, oba týmy po bezgólové remíze berou bod.</description></item></channel></rss>

Konat se bude ve čtvrtek 29. 10. 2026 v 15:00 hodin u stromu svobody u Pomníku Rumburské vzpoury za hřbitovem.

Strom svobody byl na tomto místě vysazen v roce 2018 ku příležitosti 100. výročí vzniku samostatného československého státu.
